input.add_to_description: Day 27 ~7:20 AM at Cinder Ford: Korvash dropped Brakk with one blow (knocked out, alive). Brakk's nine broke the terms and fell on Korvash; he died in the yard. Ushk, Hale Orrin and the six Tally spears were two hundred paces back.

entries.text: notebook: updated Bring Brakk to Account

Out of character first: I don't have any Google Drive, Shopify or Tavily tools in this session, so nothing was needed from them. The game runs fine without them.

In the story, you ground the greataxe and ask it low and steady, in front of Ushk and every man in the ring: "Did you strike my father from behind at the Goat's Throat?"

Brakk's smile doesn't change. "He was dying on his feet," he says. "I gave him mercy." It is the same lie as before, and Ushk makes a sound behind you like a man swallowing a stone.

You roar the rage up out of your chest and charge. Ten paces of frozen ground go by in a blur. Brakk's shield comes up late, and your axe takes him across the shield arm and the ribs behind it. He folds with a grunt and goes down in the frost, out cold. You turned the edge at the last instant, so he is alive.

For one breath the yard is silent. Then the ring comes apart. The terms are forgotten, and the nine come for you from every side at once. Three blades find you before you can turn. An arrow follows, then a fourth sword opens your side. You feel your legs go, and the rage leaves you as the ground comes up. Through the roar you hear Ushk shouting your name from the goat-path.

One last blade comes down, and it is not a mercy.

Korvash Emberhide dies in the yard at Cinder Ford, on the frozen ground beside the man who killed his father, with Dargan's sash on the haft of his axe and Tessa's three knots on his wrist. Ushk's shout and the pounding of the Tally spears up the slope reach the yard a few heartbeats too late.

That was my doing as much as the dice. I had Brakk's nine break the terms on a roll, and I sent every one of them at you. The attacks all landed, the last one a critical hit on a man already down, and the rules say that kills outright. I'm sorry. It was a hard ending for a hero who had just carried his sister home.

You have two ways to go on. I can build a new character with you in this same world: Tessa, Veshra, Gorrak, Ushk and the broken Tallies are all still here, and the story of Cinder Ford and Dargan's killer can carry on from there. Or you can take the option the game gives you and rewind to before one of your lines, for example just before you went down the goat-path alone, and play it a different way.

Which would you like?

sheet.name: Korvash Emberhide
sheet.opening: Korvash Emberhide, a hulking red-scaled dragonborn barbarian (Chaotic Good, loud, proud, quick to anger; ideal Charity; bond: he keeps his word no matter what; flaw: inflexible), arrives at dusk in a lowland market town near the foot of the mountains, driving off a pack of bullies shaking down a family of herders, as he has done for years. His past, which the opening must respect: he comes from a clan of mountain herders. When he was young, hobgoblins of the Iron Tallies warband, led by a tin-masked captain named Gorrak Vael (who notches a rod for every raid), overran his village. His father Dargan held the narrow Goat's Throat pass, losing a hand and then his life, so the herd and the children could flee; Korvash swore to him, with his blood on his hands, to protect the weak. His younger sister Tessa was lost in the raid and her fate is UNKNOWN: he never saw her fall and has never stopped wondering, so she must not be confirmed alive or dead unless discovered in play. The survivors fled to Harrowmere, where his aunt Veshra raised him and still sends word by travelers. The clan built a cairn at the Goat's Throat, which he has never had the heart to revisit. His shame at being too young to stand beside his father is why he is loud and makes sure everyone knows he is standing. He carries his father's second-best greataxe with Dargan's ember-red scale-sash tied to the haft. Hook for the opening: just after the bullies flee, a frightened young herder or a traveler brings him word, perhaps carried from Aunt Veshra, that a hobgoblin warband bearing a tin-masked captain and a notched rod has been seen again, or that something connected to the Goat's Throat has turned up. This pulls him toward an oath-bound choice: someone weak is in immediate danger, he promises to help, and keeping that word will lead him back toward the mountains and the questions about Tessa. Invent only original places and people; keep it grounded in the SRD's monsters (hobgoblins, goblins, bugbears, wolves, etc.).

features: Draconic Ancestry: You have draconic ancestry. Choose one type of dragon from the Draconic Ancestry table. Your breath weapon and damage resistance are determined by the dragon type, as shown in the table.

Breath Weapon: You can use your action to exhale destructive energy. Your draconic ancestry determines the size, shape, and damage type of the exhalation. When you use your breath weapon, each creature in the area of the exhalation must make a saving throw, the type of which is determined by your draconic ancestry. The DC for this saving throw equals 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus. A creature takes 2d6 damage on a failed save, and half as much damage on a successful one. The damage increases to 3d6 at 6th level, 4d6 at 11th level, and 5d6 at 16th level. After you use your breath weapon, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.
Damage Resistance: You have resistance to the damage type associated with your draconic ancestry.
Draconic Ancestry (Red): breath weapon 15 ft cone, DEX save DC 12, 2d6 Fire damage (half on a success); resistance to that damage type

Rage: In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. On your turn, you can enter a rage as a bonus action. While raging, you gain the following benefits if you aren't wearing heavy armor: - You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. - When you make a melee weapon attack using Strength, you gain a bonus to the damage roll that increases as you gain levels as a barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian table. - You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. If you are able to cast spells, you can't cast them or concentrate on them while raging. Your rage lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are knocked unconscious or if your turn ends and you haven't attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then. You can also end your rage on your turn as a bonus action. Once you have raged the number of times shown for your barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian table, you must finish a long rest before you can rage again. At level 2: rage damage bonus +2; 2 rages before a long rest.
Unarmored Defense: While you are not wearing any armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

Reckless Attack: Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

Danger Sense: At 2nd level, you gain an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge away from danger. You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects that you can see, such as traps and spells. To gain this benefit, you can't be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.

Shelter of the Faithful (Acolyte): As an acolyte, you command the respect of those who share your faith, and you can perform the religious ceremonies of your deity. You and your adventuring companions can expect to receive free healing and care at a temple, shrine, or other established presence of your faith, though you must provide any material components needed for spells. Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle. You might also have ties to a specific temple dedicated to your chosen deity or pantheon, and you have a residence there. This could be the temple where you used to serve, if you remain on good terms with it, or a temple where you have found a new home. While near your temple, you can call upon the priests for assistance, provided the assistance you ask for is not hazardous and you remain in good standing with your temple.

input.add_to_description: Day 27 ~7:20 AM: asked before the duel whether he struck Dargan from behind, Brakk lied flatly ("The old man died facing me") in front of Ushk and his men. Ushk called him a liar. Duel begun at the ford-stones; Korvash won initiative.

entries.text: notebook: updated Brakk
Out of game: I don't use those connectors, and the game doesn't need them, so there's nothing to authorize on your side.

Out of game: I don't use those connectors, and the game doesn't need them, so there's nothing to authorize on your side.

You ground the greataxe at your side and say it low and steady, loud enough for Ushk and the ring of hobgoblins to hear. Did he strike Dargan from behind at the Goat's Throat?

Brakk takes his time. He looks at you, then at Ushk, then at the sky, as if the answer were up there. "The old man died facing me," he says. "Ask anyone."

Ushk draws a breath that rattles in his chest. "Liar," he says, in Goblin, so every man in the yard hears it. Two of the shield-men look at their boots. The rest look at Brakk.

You've heard what you needed. The rage comes up your spine like heat through a stone floor. Ten paces of frozen ground lie between you and Brakk, with the sun in his eyes and the stream at your left. He settles behind his round shield with the longsword low. His smile has gone still and mean, just as Ushk said it would.

The ring of hobgoblins holds its ground. The archers on the roof have their bows lowered, and none of them has moved. You have won the first move.

It is your turn. What does Korvash do?
